prompt: Create a visually arresting premium editorial illustration for a software engineering article about safe retries: an order succeeded but the confirmation never arrived. Concept: THE BROKEN RETURN. On an almost-white pale mint background, a single dark ink-navy parcel sits toward the right of center. One broad cobalt-blue ribbon forms a graceful continuous outgoing path from left to right and visibly wraps across the parcel as its packing band. The returning part of the same ribbon bends back toward the left, but has a conspicuous clean missing segment, two separated ends facing each other, with a small warm coral rectangle suspended in the gap suggesting the missing confirmation. Use one continuous visual story: the parcel is there, the return path is broken. No arrowheads, no text labels, no checkmarks. Modern minimalist vector-style editorial art with strong graphic silhouettes, crisp flat shapes, subtle spatial overlap, lots of purposeful negative space. Sophisticated magazine cover rather than a generic tech diagram. Palette only ink navy, electric cobalt, pale mint and a tiny coral accent. Wide 1536x1024 with subject and path inside central 55 percent vertically to suit blog-header cropping. No typography, no letters, no code, no robots, no gradients, no 3D photorealism, no grain, no retro texture, no logos, no watermark.
